This one edit does two things the author asked for, because the tool will not let a `mock_fn` attribute and a split sit on the same function: the attribute would land on the copy left for everyone else and stop doing anything.

**The split (problem 2).** Property 17 — "the transfer CPI must debit `vault_assets_account` and credit `user_assets_account`, never the reverse" — has two halves. A recording stand-in for the wrapper shows which of the handler's accounts reach the wrapper's first and second account parameters; it cannot show what the program then does with them, because the direction lives in the argument order of the `spl_token::instruction::transfer(..)` call, whose result is a local `Instruction` with no boundary around it. `build_transfer_assets_from_vault_ix` gives that line a boundary a rule can call, so it can assert over the returned `Instruction` which pubkey lands in the source meta, which in the destination meta, and which program id is targeted — chaining with the stand-in's record to close property 17.

The split is behaviour-preserving. The builder receives exactly the `.key` values the original passed: `spl_token_program.key`, `vault_assets.key`, `user_assets.key`, and `vault_assets.key` again as the token authority — it is the same pubkey as the source, which is why the extracted function takes three keys rather than four. The `&[]` multisig list and `amount` are unchanged, the `?` still propagates the builder's `ProgramError` out of the wrapper unchanged, and `invoke_signed` is still called with the same instruction, the same three `AccountInfo` clones in the same order, and the same signer seeds. `_mint` and `vault_assets_signer_seeds` take no part in building the instruction, so they are not passed on. No check removed, no effect reordered, signature identical.

**The attribute on the replacement (problem 1).** Under `certora` + `unit_redemption` the wrapper resolves to the author's recording stand-in `crate::certora::specs::redemption::spl_transfer_assets_from_vault`, which has the identical signature, records `amount`, the keys handed to its `vault_assets`, `user_assets` and `_mint` parameters and the target program account, and returns `Ok(())`. What that drops is the wrapper's instruction construction and its `invoke_signed` of the SPL Token program, including the PDA signer seeds. The Prover already treats `solana_program::program::invoke_signed` as an unmodelled external call that moves no tokens and returns an arbitrary result — the author's last report listed it under "neither analyzed nor summarized" and the counterexample showed every token amount byte-identical across a successful `process_redeem_shares` — so no modelled asset movement is lost. Two things are gained: the handler's transfer request becomes observable (properties 3-CPI-half, 11, 17), and the call can no longer return a spurious `Err`, which is what made the acceptance rule `rule_redeem_reachable_for_legitimate_user` (property 13) unprovable.

What a reader must not conclude: under this unit nothing is proved about token balances actually moved, about the signer seeds being the correct vault-assets PDA seeds, or about errors the real builder could raise at run time inside the handler — the builder's error path is now only reachable from the rule that calls `build_transfer_assets_from_vault_ix` directly.

The inner attribute is gated on `certora` and the whole item on `unit_redemption`, so the mock exists only when both are on, as the author requires; the deployed build and every other unit compile the original function verbatim, keeping their own `unit_fee_collection` attribute. `build_transfer_assets_from_vault_ix` is `pub` in `crate::processor::spl_token_utils`, which `processor/mod.rs` declares `pub mod` and re-exports, so the harness can name it.

The same two-in-one edit as for the transfer wrapper, and for the same reason: the tool will not let a `mock_fn` attribute and a split sit on one function, because the attribute would land on the copy left for every other build and stop doing anything.

**The split (problem 2).** The author needs to assert over the `Instruction` the program's own `spl_token::instruction::burn(..)` line produces — which account ends up in which meta position and which program id it targets. That `Instruction` is a local inside `spl_burn_shares` with no boundary around it, and the only callable thing was the whole wrapper, whose `invoke` the Prover does not model. `build_burn_shares_ix` is that boundary.

The split is behaviour-preserving. The builder receives exactly the four `.key` values the original passed, in the same roles (`spl_token_program.key` as the program id, then account, mint, authority), with the same `&[]` multisig list and the same `amount`; the `?` still propagates the builder's `ProgramError` out of the wrapper unchanged; `invoke` is still called with the same instruction and the same four `AccountInfo` clones in the same order. No check removed, no effect reordered, signature identical.

**The attribute on the replacement (problem 1).** Under `certora` + `unit_redemption` the wrapper resolves to the author's recording stand-in `crate::certora::specs::redemption::spl_burn_shares`, which has the identical signature, records `amount` and the keys of the four accounts it was handed, and returns `Ok(())`. What that drops is the wrapper's instruction construction and its `invoke` of the SPL Token program. The Prover already treats `solana_program::program::invoke` as an unmodelled external call — the author's report listed it under "neither analyzed nor summarized", and the counterexample showed `user_shares_tok_before = 1697` unchanged across a successful redemption of `amount = 1` — so no modelled supply or balance effect is lost. Gained: the handler's burn request becomes observable (properties 3-CPI-half, 11, 17), and `spl_burn_shares(..)?` can no longer return an arbitrary `Err`, which is exactly what made the acceptance rule `rule_redeem_reachable_for_legitimate_user` (property 13) unprovable at handler level.

What a reader must not conclude: no rule under this unit says anything about shares actually destroyed on the token side, nor about errors the real `burn` builder could raise inside the handler — that error path is now reachable only from a rule calling `build_burn_shares_ix` directly.

The inner attribute is gated on `certora` and the whole item on `unit_redemption`, so the mock exists only when both are on; the deployed build and every other unit compile the original function verbatim, keeping their own `unit_fee_collection` attribute. `build_burn_shares_ix` is `pub` in `crate::processor::spl_token_utils`, a `pub mod` that `processor/mod.rs` re-exports, so the harness can name it.
